evidence.label: sec:p15-factorial-two-by-two, def:p15-factorial-coding: the P19 2x2 design is kept; coding x=2a-1, z=2b-1; conditional effects Delta_A(0), Delta_A(1); equal-weight average Delta_A; Delta_B defined the same way; difference of differences D_AB; normalizations D_AB/2 and D_AB/4

thm:p15-factorial-two-by-two: analysis matrix H_2 in cell order (00,10,01,11), H_2^T H_2=4I, beta=H_2^T mu/4, Delta_A=2beta_A, Delta_B=2beta_B, D_AB=4beta_AB, Delta_A(b)=2beta_A+2(2b-1)beta_AB; zero-one coding coefficients mu_00, Delta_A(0), Delta_B(0), D_AB

def:p15-factorial-retained-example: kept hypothetical means (4,0,0,2); Delta_A(0)=-4, Delta_A(1)=2, Delta_A=-1, D_AB=6; coded coefficients; explicit a with H_2^T a=c; missing cell 11 makes targets non-estimable; 'The sign difference in the original four-cell example is retained'

annex:p15.factorial.two-by-two: written derivation: orthogonality of H_2; conditional difference 2beta_A+2(2b-1)beta_AB; averaging over b cancels the interaction; differencing gives 4beta_AB; zero-one expansion; computation for the kept means

def:p19-proposed-factorial-design: the existing 2x2 design and its valid opposite-sign example (lines 645-650: means (4,0,0,2), aid-present +2 against equal-weight -1). The host keeps the same means in the same cell order
thm:p15-factorial-walsh (half-difference = 2beta_S extends the main and interaction contrasts to 2^k) and the source's Table 3.4 analysis matrix with both replicate response columns

Held source NISTSEMATECH2012DOE, physical PDF pages 1322-1323 (section 5.3.3.3.1, Table 3.4: model/analysis matrix I, X1, X2, X1*X2, X3, X1*X3, X2*X3, X1*X2*X3 with Rep 1/Rep 2 responses). Matches host lines 365-377 row for row

Held source, physical PDF page 1334 (section 5.3.3.4.1): main effect c1 is the high-setting average minus the low-setting average, 8.5, for y=(33,63,41,57,57,51,59,53). Matches host lines 558-567 and the half-difference statement of thm:p15-factorial-walsh

sec:p15-factorial-uncertainty: thm:p15-factorial-linear-uncertainty (residual degrees of freedom N-r, s^2 unbiased, exact Student interval) and thm:p15-factorial-joint-test; a zero residual degree of freedom supplies no variance estimate

thm:p15-factorial-replication: a cell mean of n_j independent runs has variance sigma^2/n_j; E[SS_pure]=(N-m)sigma^2; SSE = pure error + lack of fit. Repeated measurements on unit i give a mean with variance sigma_U^2+sigma_e^2/q. 'Four task answers from one participant are not four independently randomized participants'
thm:p15-factorial-estimability: 'Repeating existing design rows does not change which targets are estimable' (what replication cannot add)

sec:p15-factorial-randomized-blocks: source completely randomized design (90 and 369600 sequences, one-factor model) and the furnace randomized block design. thm:p15-factorial-blocks: treatment contrasts eliminate every additive block effect, variance sigma^2 sum c_t^2/B, residual df (L-1)(B-1) cannot separate interaction from pure error

thm:p15-factorial-walsh: with n replicates each effect estimate has variance sigma^2/(n2^k) and there are 2^k(n-1) pure-error df. Worked replicated source example: within-cell SS 5, pooled variance 5/8, standard error sqrt(5/32)

thm:p15-factorial-centers-blocks: in a blocked factorial the block column equals the three-factor interaction; center points in both blocks; 'Within-block replication and randomization retain their own assignment unit'

def/thm:p15-w02b-p15-075-blocked 'What blocked assignment adds': unbiased; Var = sum (N_b/N)^2 V_b depends only on within-block spread; conservative estimator needs two units per cell per block. Repeated measurements on one unit remain one assigned unit: they change Y_i(t), not N or n_t

annex:p15.factorial.replication and annex:p15.factorial.blocks: written proofs (trace argument for pure error; SSE decomposition; the unit term is not divided by q; orthogonal block and treatment spaces; block effects cancel in the contrast; residual space equals the interaction space)
annex:p15-w02b-p15-075-blocked: written proof via independent within-block complete randomizations (relies on annex:p15-w02b-p15-075-neyman, lines 60-158)

Held source, physical PDF pages 1300-1301 (section 5.3.3.1): replication and randomization in completely randomized designs (90 orderings; 12-run sequence 3,1,4,2,2,1,3,4,1,2,4,3; 369,600) and the one-factor model. Kept at host lines 203-216

Held source, physical PDF pages 1304-1306 (section 5.3.3.2): furnace-run block example (the unblocked run adds run-to-run furnace variability to error; 4x3 blocked trials; model Y=mu+T_i+B_j and its estimates). Kept at host lines 218-251

def:p15-factorial-fraction and thm:p15-factorial-alias: columns in the same word coset are identical up to sign; the normalized contrast on a fraction has expectation equal to the alias sum and estimates that sum

sec:p15-factorial-half: source Tables 3.12-3.15; principal fraction I=123 with alias classes 1=23, 2=13, 3=12; columns x3 and x1x2 coincide; replacing (beta_3,beta_12) by (beta_3+t, beta_12-t) leaves every fitted response unchanged; 'Only their sum is recovered'; negative fraction signs
def:p15-factorial-nist-effects: negative-fraction contrasts (8,16,10) equal the predicted alias differences of the full-factorial effects; the fractions estimate different sums
thm:p15-factorial-estimability: estimable iff the target is invariant on fitted-mean fibers; failure gives two parameter values with the same observation law (non-identifiability)

annex:p15.factorial.alias: written derivation (affine binary system, translation pairing); principal-fraction alias classes derived from words {empty,123}; adding t(e_3-e_12) changes neither the fitted values nor the observation law
Held source, physical PDF pages 1336-1337 (section 5.3.3.4.2): Tables 3.12-3.15 build the 2^(3-1) by setting X3 = X1*X2 (or -X1*X2). Kept at host lines 538-547

Held source, physical PDF pages 1339-1340 (section 5.3.3.4.3): 'Our computation of c3 is in fact a computation of c3 + c12'; I=123; alias set {1=23, 2=13, 3=12, I=123}; principal fraction. Kept at host lines 548-556

sec:p15-factorial-causal: def:p15-factorial-assignment and thm:p15-factorial-assignment (weighted assignment contrast unbiased for tau under stable versions, consistency, no interference, known pi_i(t)>0). P19 targets use weights (0,0,-1,1) and (-1,1,-1,1)/2. Noncompliance does not turn the assignment contrast into an effect of receipt; generalization needs a sampling or transport argument

thm:p15-factorial-mechanism: estimating the factorial surface completely does not identify the mechanism. The additional premise for a mechanism claim: process measurements with an explicit measurement model, interventions or controls that separate the competing mechanisms, and assumptions linking them to the causal equations; each claim type has its own premises
Estimability link: the explicit a solving H_2^T a=c are the weights (0,0,-1,1) and (-1,1,-1,1)/2. These are the same weights as the assignment contrasts at lines 711-712
Chapter intro: the final section separates an estimable contrast, an effect of assignment and a causal-mechanism claim

annex:p15.factorial.assignment and annex:p15.factorial.mechanism: written proofs (two finite structural models share the assignment surface 4-4A-4B+6AB but respond differently to an intervention on R)

def:p15-w02b-p15-077-study-premises: 'Under these premises the target is the assignment contrast in the recruited sample'; 'A mechanism claim needs the additional evidence described after thm:p15-factorial-mechanism'
What the results do not license: an assignment estimate concerns tau; a mechanism claim needs further premises again
Estimability is relative to a model: setting an interaction to zero can make a main effect estimable but gives no evidence that the interaction was zero (the source's sparsity premise, made explicit)

Held source, physical PDF page 1339 (section 5.3.3.4.3, sparsity of effects): the c3 computation is c3 + c12; it is acceptable only if the confounded interactions are negligible. The host states this premise at lines 52-55 and 548-556

Held source, physical PDF page 1331 (section 5.3.3.3.3): the blocking effect is the sum of block and high-order interaction effects; 'fine as long as our assumption about negligible high-order interactions holds'. The host states this as an explicit assumption at lines 463-465

defect_observations.observation: Line 552 reads 'The last two analysis columns x3, x1x2 coincide'. In the table at lines 542-547, the last two displayed columns are x3=+x1x2 and x3=-x1x2, which are negatives of each other. The sentence means x3 (principal fraction) and x1x2. This is a wording defect only; the coincident columns are visible in the table.

For the alternative 2^(8-3) (6=12345, 7=135, 8=245), the host says 24 two-factor interactions are aliased and only 12, 14, 23, 34 are clear. The held source (PDF p.1345) says 23 of 28 are confounded and lists 12, 14, 23, 27, 34 as estimable. The host's count follows from I=2467 (27=46; annex lines 333-337), so the source appears to be wrong. The host departs from the source without recording the discrepancy.

In the five-level Hyper-Graeco-Latin compact matrix, row 3 has E13. The source's compact display (PDF p.1319) prints E31, but the source's tabular run (3,4,1,3,5) (PDF pp.1318-1319) supports E13. The correction is not flagged.

The toc tag claims sections 174.1-174.4, but this chapter has no section for 174.3 (or 174.4). The 174.3 material sits in the preceding chapter sec:p15-factorial-inference (host lines 121-257 and 441-468) and in -075 lines 295-333, which the chapter introduction points to.

The introduction promises 'additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism'. The final section gives the additional evidence and premises that are needed (lines 736-741) and a nonidentification theorem; it gives no sufficient conditions for identifying the mechanism. The wording overstates the content. C04's success condition, to state the additional premise, is still met.

Two steps are left unwritten: 'The same calculation with the factors exchanged proves the formulas for B' and 'Expanding x=2a-1, z=2b-1 gives ...'. This does not block C01: its success elements (conditional, average and difference-of-differences contrasts with explicit coding) are fully derived for factor A and the AB interaction.
